source_text: CAPUT OCTAVUM. De lege cerimoniali. Haec de lege morali: Sequitur CERIMONIALIS, quae est ordinatio Dei continens praecepta de cultu Dei externo in Ecclesia V.T. observanda ad significandum, praefigurandum & obsignandum bonum promissum, & ad iuratas in conventibus & actionibus Ecclesiasticis conservandum. Hac lege Ecclesia Dei in V.T. ut infans & puella sub elementis mysteriis gubernata fuit. Vide Gal. 4:1-3; Heb. 8:5; 10:1; Col. 2:14, 11.
english: CHAPTER EIGHT. On the ceremonial law.

After the moral law follows the CEREMONIAL, which is an ordinance of God containing precepts concerning the external worship of God to be observed in the Old Testament Church, for signifying, prefiguring, and sealing the promised good, and for preserving the sworn order in ecclesiastical assemblies and actions.
By this law God's Church in the Old Testament was governed as an infant and a girl under elemental mysteries (Gal. 4:1-3; Heb. 8:5; 10:1; Col. 2:14, 11).

source_text: II. Ejus praecepta, quantumvis varia, tamen ad quatuor classes potissimum referri possunt: sacramenta, sacrificia, sacra, & legales observationes. De sacramentis inferius suo loco dicetur. Sacrificium vero est externa sacra actio, qua res aliqua sensibilis, permanens, a legitimo ministro Deo proxime offertur, ad testificandum supremum illius dominium & hominis subjectionem. Dividi autem possunt sacrificia quadriariam: 1. ratione materiae (animal / inanimis; holocaustum, immolatio, libamen); 2. ex forma (holocaustum, hostia pacifica, hostia pro peccato); 3. ex parte rei oblatae (cruentum / incruentum); 4. ex fine (latreuticum, eucharisticum, impetratorium, hilasticum). Per sacra intelliguntur personae sacrae, loca, tempus, vasa, instrumenta cultus. Observationes legales erant ceremoniae ad pacificationem & sanctificationem pertinentes, quibus ab infidelibus discernebantur.
english: II. Its precepts, however varied, may chiefly be referred to four classes: sacraments, sacrifices, sacred things, and legal observances. Of the sacraments we will speak below in their place.

A sacrifice is an external sacred action by which some sensible, permanent thing is offered immediately to God by a lawful minister, to testify His supreme dominion and the human's subjection. Sacrifices are divided four ways: by matter, by form, by bloody or unbloody offering, and by particular end (latreutic, eucharistic, petitionary, or propitiatory).

By sacred things are meant sacred persons and all else required for external worship. Legal observances were ceremonies of pacification and sanctification by which they were distinguished from unbelievers.

source_text: III. Est autem observandus legis ceremonialis usus & abrogatio. IV. Usus illius fuit 1. ut populum veterem sub spe & expectatione promissorum bonorum contineret; 2. ut populum Israeliticum a reliquis gentibus discerneret tanquam paries intergerinus, donec diruta maceria per adventum Christi cum iis in unum corpus coalescerent; 3. ut isto operoso cultu occupati neque cultus alios ipsi confingerent neque ab aliis confictos usurparent. Primum usum praestat per typos, figuras, umbras. Hoc respectu lex illa iure merito paedagogus ad Christum appellatur. Vide Heb. 10:1-3; Col. 2:14, 17; Gal. 3:24; Eph. 2:14-15.
english: III. The use and abrogation of the ceremonial law are to be observed. IV. Its use was: 1. to hold the ancient people under hope of the promised goods; 2. to distinguish Israel from the nations by a middle wall until Christ tore it down and they coalesced into one body; 3. that occupied with this laborious worship they might neither invent other cults nor take up those invented by others.
The first use it performs through types, figures, and shadows. In this respect that law is rightly called a pedagogue to Christ (Heb. 10:1-3; Col. 2:14, 17; Gal. 3:24; Eph. 2:14-15).

source_text: V. Abrogata est lex cerimonialis per Christi crucem, mortem, resurrectionem, ascensionem in coelos & missionem Spiritus; per umbrarum a sole depulsionem & corporis earum locum successionem. Abrogata est quantum ad necessitatem observandi, omni iure obligandi simul & semel adempto; et hoc ipso viva esse desinit & mortua est. Abolenda fuit ipso facto partim per doctrinam Apostolorum, partim per potentiam Dei in destructione Hierosolymorum & templi. Ex quo tempore ceremoniae illae coeperunt esse mortiferae quae intermedio spatio fuerunt tolerabiles inter Judaeos duntaxat. Vide Col. 2:11-17; Gal. 4:9-10; Acts 16:3; 21:22-24; Gal. 2:3, 11-12. CAPUT NONUM sequitur, De lege forensi.
english: V. The ceremonial law was abrogated through Christ's cross, death, resurrection, ascension, and the sending of the Spirit—by the sun driving away the shadows and the body succeeding into their place.

It is abrogated as to the necessity of observing it, every right of obligation being taken away at once; and by this it ceases to be living and is dead. It was abolished in fact partly by the Apostles' teaching and partly by God's destruction of Jerusalem and the temple. From then those ceremonies became deadly which had been tolerable only among Jews in the intervening space (Col. 2:11-17; Gal. 4:9-10; Acts 16:3; 21:22-24).
CHAPTER NINE follows, On the forensic law.
